source_title: James Cropper PLC Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 39 and 43 state that the report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 24 June 2019; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue reached a record £101.1m, but adjusted operating profit fell to £4.3m from £6.1m and profit before tax fell 43% to £2.6m. Paper incurred a £2.0m loss after £6.5m of cumulative pulp-cost pressure and further energy inflation, while the developing 3D Products business also lost money. Net borrowings rose to £8.6m and the pension deficit widened, though TFP profit grew 19%, EBITDA retained covenant headroom and management had already announced margin-recovery and operational plans.
already_announced_exclusion: Paper price, mix, energy and cost-recovery measures; portfolio optimisation; operational reorganisation; and announced investment actions were public or underway before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Severe divisional losses, cost under-recovery and a sharp profit decline produce a strong pressure signal, moderated by record revenue, highly profitable TFP and covenant headroom; disclosed recovery actions are excluded.

source_title: James Cropper PLC Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 25, 35, 36 and 40 state that the report and financial statements were approved by the Board on 23 August 2023; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 24% to £129.7m through volume, pricing and energy surcharges, but adjusted profit before tax fell 21% to £3.2m and statutory profit before tax fell to £1.3m from £2.8m. Paper's adjusted operating loss widened to £2.8m and Colourform lost £1.1m amid energy and raw-material volatility; net debt rose to £16.6m and gearing to 38%. TFP profit increased, demand remained strong and the Group had already implemented pricing, commercial-leadership and strategic actions.
already_announced_exclusion: Energy surcharges, pricing, commercial-leadership changes, portfolio repositioning and other strategic or operational actions disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Strong demand and revenue growth coexist with weaker profit, persistent divisional losses and rising leverage, creating material pressure moderated by TFP strength and already-implemented recovery actions.
